disclaimer: All verdicts are early editorial calls from public documentation and pricing. early:true means not yet run on a full New Wave creative-director brief. No fabricated test results, quotes, stats, or testimonials.
header: The AI stack for professional designers.
positioning: NwWv is an AI-integrated design agency, weekly newsletter, and active community for today's creative professional figuring out a new generation of tools.

tools.name: Recraft
tools.summary: One of the few generators that returns real, editable SVG instead of a PNG to retrace. Custom styles lock a visual language so icon sets and marks stay consistent. Treat every output as a sketch to finish in Illustrator.
tools.whoFor: Identity and brand designers who need a mark, icon set, or pattern system in vector, quickly.
strengths: Native SVG / vector output
Custom styles for brand-consistent families
V4.1 Flash for fast cheap iteration; Refine when something is worth keeping
Studio now hosts other labs' models (e.g. ChatGPT Images, Seedance) alongside Recraft models
weaknesses: Output is a starting file, not a finished mark (curves, kerning, anchors still need craft)
Free plan: images are public, not licensed for commercial use
tools.price: Basic $12/mo or $10/mo annual; Pro from $20/mo or $16 annual; Teams from $22/mo or $18/seat annual. API Flash $0.007; V4.1 vector $0.08.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.summary: When the job lives or dies on legible type, start here. Expect raster output, so a wordmark still needs vectorizing and kerning by hand.
tools.whoFor: Designers making wordmarks, posters, and type-led social graphics.
strengths: Reliable in-image text compared with most generators
Useful for posters and social where the words are the layout
API available for a workflow once the look is approved
weaknesses: Raster, not vector
A wordmark still needs a designer's kerning and outlines
tools.price: Free 30 credits/week (Google, Apple, or Microsoft sign-in). Plus $20/mo ($15 annual), Pro $60/mo ($42 annual), Team $30/user/mo ($20 annual).

tools.name: Looka
tools.summary: A template-driven logo maker for founders who don't have a designer. Paying for the files buys a starting point weaker than a short sketch.
tools.whoFor: Not for working designers. Built for small businesses buying a logo file and a brand-kit template.
strengths: Fast preview if a non-designer needs any mark at all
One-time file purchase instead of a subscription
weaknesses: Template logic, not art direction
The paid files are still a starting point a designer would redraw
Confirm looka.com/pricing before publishing; figures below come from Looka's help pages and a third-party summary
tools.price: Free to design and preview. Basic logo $20 one-time (one low-res PNG). Premium $65 one-time (hi-res + vector). Brand Kit $96/yr.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.summary: Still the fastest way to explore a look before you commit to a shoot or an illustrator. Budget for Pro on client work: there is no API, and the gallery is public unless you pay for stealth.
tools.whoFor: Art directors exploring style, references, and campaign looks.
strengths: Strong aesthetics and style references
Fast look-development before a shoot or an illustrator
Omni reference for holding a direction across frames
weaknesses: No API
Public gallery unless you are on Pro or Mega (stealth)
Plan docs say companies with more than $1M gross revenue a year need Pro or Mega; check the terms before publishing
The video mode is a separate, weaker call and is not why this verdict is Use
tools.price: Basic $10/mo, Standard $30, Pro $60, Mega $120 (20% off annual). No free tier.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.summary: If you already live in Photoshop and Illustrator, this is the least disruptive way to add generative work to client ads. Adobe's own Firefly models are the conservative pick for commercial use.
tools.whoFor: Designers already in Creative Cloud who need image, vector, and Generative Fill inside the files they deliver.
strengths: Generative Fill, text to vector, and image tools inside the apps you already hand off from
Adobe's own models are the clearer commercial-use path
Partner models (Gemini, GPT Image, FLUX, Ideogram, Runway, Kling) available in one place
weaknesses: Partner models carry their own terms, and some are not on business plans yet
Plan prices below are from a third-party summary; check adobe.com before publishing
tools.price: Free tier. Standard $9.99/mo (2,000 credits), Pro $19.99, Pro Plus $49.99, Premium $199.99. Standard generations are unlimited on paid plans; premium and partner features use credits.

tools.name: AdCreative.ai
tools.summary: Built for volume, not craft. Output reads templated, credits get pricey per download, and its conversion score isn't something we can verify. Designers get better variants from Firefly or Canva with real art direction.
tools.whoFor: Not a designer's production tool. Aimed at people who want scored ad volume from a brand kit.
strengths: Fast volume from a brand kit if craft is not the point
weaknesses: Output reads templated
Credits get pricey as downloads add up
The conversion score is a claim we cannot verify
No clean /pricing URL. Plan rungs are cited at $39, $249, and $999; Starter credit counts disagree across sources (10 vs 20). Confirm on send day
tools.price: Trial cited as 7 days. Plans cited from $39/mo up to $999/mo, with discounts on longer billing. Do not publish the credit count until it is confirmed on the vendor's own page.

tools.name: Canva AI
tools.summary: For a high-volume social calendar with a brand kit, nothing in-house moves faster. Use it for production and resizing, not for concepting the brand itself.
tools.whoFor: Designers producing and resizing social sets from an existing brand kit.
strengths: Brand Kit, Magic Resize, and template production at volume
Useful once the concept already exists
weaknesses: Not where a brand gets its point of view
Canva changed Pro pricing and free AI limits in Sept 2026; recheck AI-use counts on canva.com/pricing
tools.price: Free plan. Pro US$144/yr per person (US pricing, Sept 2026). AI use limits depend on tier.

tools.name: Framer
tools.summary: It ships a real, responsive, hosted site that a designer fully controls, which most AI website builders do not. Wireframer gives you a starting layout. The craft stays with you.
tools.whoFor: Designers who need a hosted marketing site or landing page they can still design by hand.
strengths: Designer-grade layout control plus hosting
Wireframer for a starting page, Workshop for AI components
The file remains editable after the prompt
weaknesses: AI credits are a starting boost, not the site
A generated layout still needs type, spacing, and content editing
tools.price: Free (one-time 500 AI credits). Basic $10/mo, Pro $30/mo per site, billed annually.

tools.name: Figma Make
tools.summary: Useful for clickable prototypes from frames you already have, and it lives in a tool the team pays for. Generated layouts and code still need a designer's cleanup.
tools.whoFor: Product and brand teams who already work in Figma and want a prototype, not a shipped site.
strengths: Uses existing Figma files as context
Included with Full seats, so there is no second subscription to trial the idea
weaknesses: Generated code and layout still need cleanup
AI credits can run out quickly on big iterations
Not a replacement for a designed, hosted page
tools.price: Included with Figma Full seats (Professional plan about 3,000 AI credits/mo per Full seat). Extra credits sold separately.

tools.name: Runway
tools.summary: The most complete production toolkit for short-form brand video: editing, references, and consistency controls beyond plain text-to-video. Credits go fast, so prototype before you render the finals.
tools.whoFor: Designers and directors making short brand films, product loops, and campaign motion.
strengths: Gen-4.5 / Gen-4 video plus Aleph editing
References, 4K upscale, and third-party models in the same project
Closer to a timeline than a one-shot generator
weaknesses: Credits go fast. Gen-4.5 is 12 credits per second
The Unlimited plan is being retired; legacy subscribers move to Max on Nov 30, 2026
tools.price: Free 125 one-time credits. Standard $12/mo, Pro $28/mo, Max $76/mo, billed annually.

tools.name: Kling
tools.summary: Motion quality competes with the best, with native audio and high resolution. Watch stands: as of Oct 15, 2026, Flash is limited early access and full 4.0 is still described as launching or rolling out this October.
tools.whoFor: Directors who want another motion option once access and data terms are clear. Not for client footage yet.
strengths: Strong motion, native audio, multi-shot, up to 4K on the versions already described
Worth another look when 4.0 is actually generally available
weaknesses: Full 4.0 was not a finished public launch as of Oct 15, 2026
First-month promo pricing and enterprise data terms need a check before client footage goes in
Adobe currently restricts Kling to individual plans only
tools.price: Free basic tier. Standard $8.80/mo, Pro $32.56/mo, Premier $80.96/mo, Ultra $159.99/mo, with a lower intro first month. Recheck kling.ai on send day; these figures are from public pages and may predate 4.0.

tools.name: Krea
tools.summary: The real-time canvas is a genuine ideation tool for art directors. It is an aggregator of other labs' models, so the result depends on which model you pick. We will look again after it has been run on a full brief.
tools.whoFor: Art directors who want a live canvas for concepts, not a single-model pipeline.
strengths: Real-time generation canvas
Multi-model image and video, upscaling, and custom training in one place
weaknesses: Quality tracks whichever underlying model you select
Not yet run on a full New Wave brief, so the verdict stays Watch
tools.price: Free 100 units/day. Basic $9/mo, Pro $35/mo, Max $105/mo, Business $200/mo (about 40% off annual).
